heading: Do optimizer and numerical artifacts fully explain the grokking delay?
definition: the delay is produced by optimizer or numerical choices (adaptive-optimizer instabilities, floating-point limits in the softmax) and disappears when those are controlled.
summary: The claim that controlling optimizer behavior and numerical effects eliminates grokking delays is contested. Delays persist under plain gradient descent and precision controls, while stabilizing numerical calculations can enable delayed grokking.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for the unrestricted artifact explanation in toy and synthetic settings. Explicit parameter-count buckets <1B, 1–10B, 10–100B and >100B remain unassessed: counts versions.V7.studies_by_size records only 'not stated'.
suggested_status.reason: Optimizer and numerical interventions affect grokking, but the unrestricted disappearance claim is challenged by persistence under vanilla GD/MSE (arXiv:2310.06110#R17), delayed grokking enabled by numerical stabilization (arXiv:2501.04697#r10), and matched precision audits retaining delay (arXiv:2606.18465#r41). Corrected cross-entropy qualitatively accelerates grokking in modular-addition transformers, establishing a numerical contribution to slower grokking, not production and complete removal of the delay (arXiv:2610.31642#R19). Its endpoint comparison cannot establish disappearance or persistence of the post-memorization delay (arXiv:2610.31642#R24). counts: versions.V7.verdicts.supports.studies=4; versions.V7.verdicts.challenges.studies=16; versions.V7.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=4. These overlapping source tallies precede the checker's reclassification of arXiv:2610.31642's supports verdict to limits_scope; they are not corrected totals or independent replication counts.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched intervention that removes a specified instability or rounding mechanism, preserves learning capability, and quantifies the remaining post-memorization lag would delimit the causal claim. Repeating that test across tasks and explicit model scales would establish its scope.

source.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
source.authors: Neel Nanda; Lawrence Chan; Tom Lieberum; J. Smith; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The study compared grokking with slingshot behavior (repeated sudden loss spikes late in training) in 1-layer transformers with regularization.
original_result.result: Many 1-layer models grokked without slingshots (repeated sudden loss spikes late in training), showing that slingshots are unnecessary for grokking with weight decay or other regularization.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Optimizer settings that suppressed Slingshot also eliminated grokking and prevented generalization.
Removing the gradient component that scales logits under cross-entropy eliminated the delay attributed to that scaling.
A method largely eliminated delays on modular addition and shortened them on tasks computing x²+y.
Rounding errors in softmax slowed grokking and lowered accuracy, especially without weight decay.
Stabilizing modular-addition training greatly shortened the delay but preserved distinct memorization and generalization transitions.
Only Adam initially stayed at chance accuracy; optimizer choice did not eliminate the delay.
Numerical collapse persisted with scheduled SGD, without adaptive moments.
Fixing numerical errors in the cross-entropy loss sped up grokking, but generalization was still delayed.
Parity grokking occurred with plain SGD and hinge loss, without adaptive optimizers or softmax.
Normalized classifiers grokked on modular division without training instability.
Delayed generalization persisted under plain gradient descent at learning rates chosen to exclude instability.
Grokking persisted with vanilla gradient descent and MSE, without adaptive optimizers or softmax.
Reducing training spikes slowed generalization but preserved the delay.
Delayed generalization occurred under vanilla gradient descent and analytically under gradient flow.
Full-batch gradient descent retained delayed generalization with an explicit penalty mimicking Adam's implicit bias.
Sparse recovery and matrix completion retained long delays without adaptive optimizers or softmax.
Controlling softmax numerical errors enabled grokking, but generalization was still delayed.
Grokking occurred with momentum-free SGD and squared loss instead of cross-entropy.
Plain SGD produced grokking at larger scales for model outputs, without an adaptive optimizer.
Exact gradient flow and vanilla gradient descent produced closely matching delays without softmax.
Normalizing the output layer preserved long delays on modular addition and multiplication.
Ridge regression provably generalized after a delay in exact arithmetic, without adaptive optimizers or softmax.
Float64 softmax removed Slingshot spikes while grokking persisted.
Higher numerical precision preserved the delay or prevented early grokking, depending on the setting.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Artifact-controlled delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning, including named large-model families and explicit parameter-count scales.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V7.studies_by_family contains only 'other or not stated'; versions.V7.studies_by_size contains only 'not stated'; versions.V7.studies_by_stage and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation contain no base or fine-tuned coverage. The precision studies listed here concern small modular-arithmetic models.

untested.what: A matched factorial experiment separating adaptive-optimizer instabilities from softmax rounding, while retaining successful generalization and quantifying the remaining delay.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines for arXiv:2206.04817 leave precision untested; arXiv:2501.04697 leaves slingshot instabilities unmeasured; arXiv:2606.18465 leaves adaptive-optimizer instabilities untested. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation records training and measurement but provides no joint mechanism-control breakdown. The checker also identifies adaptive-optimizer instability and floating-point mechanisms as untested in the one-layer modular-arithmetic transformer comparisons arXiv:2505.11411#r7 and arXiv:2505.11411#r21; optimizer-dependent shortening or disappearance does not isolate those mechanisms.

untested.what: A numerical measurement establishing whether corrected cross-entropy reduces the interval from training-accuracy saturation to generalization to zero.
untested.basis: Pipeline assessment: no numerical training-saturation-to-generalization interval is reported. arXiv:2610.31642#R1 reports final accuracy; arXiv:2610.31642#R19 gives a qualitative timing comparison in Figure 2, establishing faster grokking with corrected cross-entropy without establishing complete removal of the delay. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation and versions.V7.rows_by_evidence_form do not resolve this timing gap.

untested.what: Direct tests establishing whether normalization and batch-size interventions control adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point softmax effects in the reported modular-addition transformers.
untested.basis: arXiv:2308.09543#R10 adds layer normalization and reduces batch size while retaining AdamW; overall convergence accelerates and separate memorization and generalization transitions remain, but the checker finds V7's mechanisms untested. arXiv:2603.05228#UNEMBED-CONTROL reports prolonged memorization with normalized unembedding alone; retained internal radial freedom prevents treating this as an established numerical control, and adaptive-optimizer instabilities remain uncontrolled. counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation provides no breakdown establishing these mechanism controls.

wording_issues.phrase: the delay is produced by optimizer or numerical choices
wording_issues.issue: The wording generalizes a causal explanation across settings. Delays also occur under vanilla GD with MSE and in exact-arithmetic ridge-regression analysis. Optimizer dependence in particular experiments does not establish a universal artifact origin.

Removing slingshot spikes can leave grokking intact. In one-layer transformers on addition modulo 67 with a 50% training split, WanD largely eliminates the delay; both optimizers generalize after approximately 2,000 optimization steps. On x²+y modulo 67 with a 50% training fraction, WanD/AdamW annealing shortens the delay, only partially supporting disappearance. Neither comparison tests adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point mechanisms. Orthogonal-gradient interventions remove the delay without weight decay in the reported subtraction-modulo-113 transformer and addition-modulo-113 MLP runs; their proposed mechanism is cross-entropy-driven logit scaling rather than adaptive-optimizer instability.

The numerical effects have different consequences across conditions: Collapse can prevent generalization, a precision-cliff bug can slow it, and float32 Collapse can produce an earlier spurious grok. Corrected cross-entropy qualitatively speeds grokking in the fp32 modulo-31 transformer setting with weight decay λ=1, establishing a numerical contribution to slower grokking without establishing production and complete removal of the delay. These findings support a qualified artifact account.

In unregularized algorithmic transformers, suppressing grokking through Adam epsilon changes or momentum-SGD controls is directionally consistent with optimizer dependence, but those runs also fail to generalize. This does not demonstrate removal of the memorization phase while retaining successful generalization. Casting logits to float64 before log_softmax removes slingshot spikes while grokking persists. Corrected fp32 cross-entropy matching the fp64 reference and reaching 100% final accuracy establishes an endpoint result; that row cannot determine disappearance or persistence of the post-memorization delay. The qualitative corrected-cross-entropy timing comparison establishes faster grokking without quantifying a zero residual lag.

method_sensitivity.what: One-layer modular-addition transformers retain delayed generalization under full-batch GD with explicit ℓ∞ regularization, contradicting adaptive-optimizer necessity. In the WanD comparison on addition modulo 67, the general setup specifies a 50% training/test split; both optimizers generalize after approximately 2,000 optimization steps, while WanD largely eliminates the delay. Separately, WanD/AdamW annealing shortens the delay on x²+y modulo 67, providing only partial evidence for disappearance. The studies differ in optimizer, modulus, training data and regularization, and the x²+y comparison changes the task. These are conditional method differences rather than a matched conflict; the WanD comparisons do not isolate adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point mechanisms.

method_sensitivity.factor: Adam epsilon, weight decay and capability preservation
method_sensitivity.what: In unregularized algorithmic transformers, changing Adam epsilon can suppress both slingshots and generalization. At epsilon=10^-5, grokking and successful generalization are absent after 500K updates. Momentum-SGD controls likewise suppress Slingshot and grokking but fail to generalize. These outcomes support optimizer dependence without demonstrating immediate successful generalization. Separately, zero-weight-decay runs exhibit Slingshot and grokking; stronger weight decay removes Slingshot and the delayed transition while permitting rapid high validation accuracy. Appendix C.1 nevertheless reports persistent training instability under stronger decay, so removing Slingshot must not be equated with eliminating all instability.

method_sensitivity.factor: Precision, cross-entropy implementation and margin regime
method_sensitivity.what: Casting logits to float64 before log_softmax removes spikes while preserving grokking in the full-batch AdamW transformer reported by lw:N6WM6hs7RQMKDhYjB. In arXiv:2501.04697, higher precision can postpone Collapse, but float64 does not restore grokking at the 40% training split. The modular-addition MLP audit in arXiv:2606.18465 preserves delayed grokking in one precision comparison and removes a spurious early transition in another; eventual float64 generalization in the latter is unestablished. In arXiv:2610.31642, corrected cross-entropy accelerates grokking in the reported fp32 modular-addition transformer comparison without establishing complete removal of the delay. Its fp64 comparisons below the precision cliff establish no final-accuracy benefit, not equivalence of delay lengths; those endpoint rows are cannot_determine for V7.

Orthogonal-to-weight gradient projection removes the initial overfitting phase under both AdamW and SGD in the reported modular-arithmetic transformer and MLP experiments. These projected-gradient runs use no weight decay under the Section 2.2 default; the weight-decay baseline is a separate comparison. StableMax experiments in the same study instead permit delayed grokking. Optimizer geometry and numerical stabilization have distinct outcomes.

In synthetic linear classification, GD supports delayed generalization while Adam produces a more canonical chance-level initial plateau. Persistence under ordinary GD contradicts V7's predicted disappearance under nonadaptive optimization. The Adam plateau establishes descriptive curve-shape sensitivity but does not identify an optimizer instability or numerical artifact; that example alone is cannot_determine for V7.

In the modular-addition MLP output-scale sweep, increasing scale produces grokking under SGD, while LM substantially alleviates the delay. These optimizer outcomes must be separated despite their shared extracted rows. The available text does not establish individual curve geometry or complete disappearance of the delay under LM.

Changing AdamW beta2 to 0.98 and adding 10-step warmup changes reported grokking outcomes but does not remove slingshots. The B2-frz condition groks in 4/5 seeds, making its V1 outcome partial rather than uniformly observed. Default-setting and attempted-stabilization rows are all cannot_determine for V7: persistent instability prevents them from establishing whether successfully controlling it removes the delay.

In a one-layer autoregressive modular-addition transformer retaining AdamW, adding layer normalization and reducing batch size from 2048 to 256 yields approximately 30 times faster overall convergence. The memorization–generalization gap is dramatically reduced, while separate memorization and generalization transitions remain; the speedup does not measure the gap reduction. Figure 5's caption also mentions a lower learning rate, whereas Section 3.3 and Table 6 identify normalization and batch-size changes; this discrepancy remains unresolved. These interventions do not isolate adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits: V7 is cannot_determine and receives no verdict.
